title: Motion and Kinematics Simulator — Overview and definition
t: Motion and Kinematics Simulator — Overview and definition
description: Simulates positions, velocities, and accelerations of mechanisms over time.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Simulates positions, velocities, and accelerations of mechanisms over time. A motion and kinematics simulator computes forward and inverse kinematics of linkages, cams, and gear trains, then animates joint trajectories with velocity and acceleration profiles. Real implementations use Denavit-Hartenberg parameters, screw theory, or recursive Newton-Euler formulations, and export motion profiles to controllers. It detects singularities, joint-limit violations, and collisions along a path.
capabilities: Forward and inverse kinematics for serial and parallel mechanisms
Trajectory generation with trapezoidal and S-curve profiles
Singularity, joint-limit, and self-collision detection
Velocity and acceleration analysis at any point of the cycle
Export of motion programs to robot and motion controllers

body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Teaching ladder for Motion and Kinematics Simulator, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Forward and inverse kinematics for serial and parallel mechanisms). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Forward and inverse kinematics for serial and parallel mechanisms and Trajectory generation with trapezoidal and S-curve profiles. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Robot kinematics solver) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
